_comment: Consensus Edge parameters, v1.
PROVENANCE OF EVERY NUMBER IN THIS FILE, because the difference
matters more than the values themselves:
measured  - derived from an out-of-sample result committed under
docs/measurements/. Quote these.
prior     - a starting value chosen for a stated reason, never
validated. Do NOT quote these as findings.
The composite weights are PRIORS. Market Mispricing has an
out-of-sample result (rho +0.089/+0.126/+0.111 across 7/14/30-day
horizons, 24 non-overlapping folds); Sharp Flow and Opportunity do
not, because neither has data to validate against in any
environment without the prod-only data/intel ledger. A weight fitted
against one measured component and two unmeasured ones would encode
guesses as if they were findings, so the weights below are declared
and labelled rather than fitted.
This is why the consensus_edge feature flag defaults OFF and why
components are reported separately in every payload.
Do not edit in place once a paramSetId has shipped values - the id
is a content hash, so any edit produces a new id and stored results
stay attributable to the params that produced them.

_rationale: Mispricing carries the most weight because it is the only
component with an out-of-sample number. Sharp Flow is second
because qualified-manager behaviour is genuinely independent
evidence when it exists. Opportunity is smallest because it
mostly confirms whether a gap will persist rather than
establishing one.
Weights are renormalised over PRESENT components only, so a
player with no sharp data is not silently scored as though sharp
evidence were neutral - see score.py::composite.
Bands are symmetric and round. They are NOT calibrated: with a
single validated component there is no basis for asserting that
+60 means anything different in kind from +55. They exist to make
the score readable, and the UI labels them experimental.
A score near zero has two completely different meanings: nothing
is happening, or strong evidence is cancelling. Averaging them to
the same number is the single most misleading thing a composite
can do, so opposing components above this magnitude force the
Conflicted label regardless of the arithmetic.
Beta(1,1) is a uniform prior: with no observations the posterior
mean is 0.5, i.e. direction 0.0, which is the honest answer.
The recency half-life and the caps address defects measured on
main: today's signal applies no per-manager or per-league cap at
all, so one active manager in ten leagues contributes ten
observations. maxManagerShare/maxLeagueShare bound any single
contributor's influence on one asset.
A geometric mean, so a single zeroed factor collapses the whole
score. That is deliberate: confidence is a conjunction - fresh
data AND adequate coverage AND agreement - and an arithmetic mean
would let three strong factors hide one absent one.
